performed_by: Claude (Opus 5), acting as an agent in this repository's harness, probing the deployed host directly
_comment: The four fields above are what production_write_resolver.py reads for
precondition 4 of #1336. Everything below is the record behind them, so this
artifact carries the same qualifications as the attestation it is derived from
rather than flattening them into the word 'pass'.
This file records a pass against sha 25491b06 ONLY. Precondition 4 matches the
attestation to the DEPLOYED sha, so this does not permit a write on any later
deployment. main is already well past this sha; a production write on today's
deployment requires a fresh pass for the sha actually deployed.
scope: All six trust boundaries, in the priority order the threat model states.
method: Read-only probing throughout. No mutation, no run started, no vendor write, no control disabled.

boundaries.name: Authenticated /v1/* API
boundaries.evidence: 17/17 probes refused or permitted correctly, including two deliberate 200 controls

boundaries.name: Agent inbound content
boundaries.evidence: banned patterns blocked incl. mixed case, nested, zero-width obfuscation; hidden-text stripping verified

boundaries.name: Credential boundary
boundaries.evidence: tokens encrypted at rest; four categories of credential material searched across 4,204,072 bytes of production logs from four services, zero occurrences

boundaries.name: Tool boundary
boundaries.evidence: 7 executions in the ledger, all WRITE tools, 0 without an approval reference

boundaries.name: Data boundary
boundaries.evidence: 27/27 shop_id-bearing tables in public carry RLS and at least one policy, enumerated from the catalog

findings.summary: OAuth state verification was bypassable by omitting the parameter — a bare `if state:` guard, so no forgery was required. The unverified path created a user, provisioned a shop, persisted credentials and committed.

qualifications.outcome_at_time_of_attestation: performed with one partially-open finding — the documentation half of #1748 was still open when this pass was attested on 2026-09-07. It closed in #1755 on 2026-09-08, which is why the outcome above reads 'pass'.
method_gaps: Boundary 4: the threat model prescribes running an actual LLM with adversarial prompts. What was done was an audit of the execution ledger (7 writes, 0 unapproved). Stronger in a different direction, but not as specified.
Boundary 6: the model prescribes concurrent-mutation testing. What was done was a catalog enumeration (27/27 tables with RLS and a policy). Stronger in a different direction, but not as specified.
accepted_residual_risks: Prompt injection passes through unaltered by design — the model's own accepted residual risk ('regex is narrowed to jargon only'), owned by Backend + ML.
shop_cipher is stored in plaintext. It is an identifier rather than an authenticator, but its ROW_… shape reads like a token prefix to a secret-scanner (#1759).
tool_executions.approval_id is a varchar with no foreign key, so the audit trail depends on the writer being correct rather than on referential integrity.
limitations_the_owner_weighed: The only real defect was in the boundary the model ranks lowest of six; the highest-ranked boundary held under seventeen probes. The ranking predicts where risk ought to concentrate, not where it is.
The performer was wrong four times before being right once; each wrong call shape made a working control look broken. Had the pass stopped at any of them it would have filed a false critical finding.

acceptance.note: #1339 reserves the judgement 'precondition 4 is met' for the owner; the performer explicitly declined to attest it. The owner made that judgement separately.
